title: Beni Mellal city and foothills, 2 Sep to 26 Sep 2026
summary: From 2 Sep to 26 Sep 2026 the radar shows 1.51 km2 turning brighter in HV around Beni Mellal, against 0.42 km2 darker. The changing fields hold most of the brighter area, 1.13 km2.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 24 days mean HV rose by 0.07 dB and mean HH moved by -0.02 dB. In HV, 1.51 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.42 km2 darker; in HH, 1.71 km2 turned brighter and 0.39 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The changing fields rose 1.03 dB in HV and 1.34 dB in HH on average. Rough dry ground and fields had 0.19 km2 brighter in HV and rose 0.1 dB. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes had 0.12 km2 brighter and 0.1 km2 darker, and built-up land rose 0.08 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the brighter fields: crops growing through September, which adds volume scattering; a field visit would confirm it. Possible cause for the few darker patches: plots harvested or cleared; the optical photo would show them.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow. Small patches are close to what speckle alone can produce at the 3 dB threshold.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: A farm office could compare the 1.13 km2 of brighter fields with its sowing records. The city itself stayed stable, so this pair is a clean view of field activity.
